text.text_excerpt: Oohh lala. I know Bourbon gets all the press, but honestly Royal Street is the best window shopping/gallery hopping street in NOLA. First off it's pedestrian only during the day so you don't have to be worried about getting run over which is nice.* Galleries feature art for every taste and just about every price point. There are clothing shops, accessory shops, antiques, housewares, restaurants, bars (of course), hotels and homes. The architecture is great. And on a hot summer day, there's usually enough shade that you won't melt into the sidewalk. Definitely plan to stroll the 13 blocks of Royal in the FQ from Canal to Esplanade. Each one offers something different from tourist kitsch to...

I have some bias because my hotel was on this street (Hotel Monteleone) BUT Royal Street is also host to some amazing eateries, stores, and local flavor. This is definitely one of the more upscale streets in New Orleans where you can also get some good people-watching in. Street performers, artists, boutiques and more! Plus, all the main attractions in New Orleans are in walking distance from this quaint street. I love that it hosts so much local flare without the craziness that inhabits Bourbon Street (lol). Kind of a similar vibe to Frenchmen Street, but Frenchmen Street is more the place to go at night. :) Royal Street is certainly refreshing if you're tired of the party scene in New O...

Royal Street gets my vote for "Best Street in the French Quarter". You can find art galleries, boutiques, antiques, shoes, accessories, tourist traps, restaurants, bars, a museum, some amazing architecture, and a constantly changing array of street performers. Some parts of Royal street are blocked of from vehicular traffic from 11-4pm which allows you to wander around and shop and soak in all that this great street has to offer.
